1.falsification: Equivalent terminal-index implementations should agree. Disagreement indicates implementation or evaluation uncertainty. If recent-state aggregation consistently fails to outperform the corrected terminal-only control, the aggregation hypothesis is unsupported. A correctness-fix improvement alone is not evidence for an architecture gain. Execution failures do not falsify the mechanism.
1.hypothesis: Selecting the actual final valid state will improve alignment between prediction and the observed history. Aggregating a small number of recent valid states may additionally improve validation HR@10 by reducing sensitivity to the terminal state. Compare architecture candidates against the corrected terminal-only artifact separately from untouched baseline trial 0 (HR@10 0.395). The controller performs all frozen training and evaluation; retain candidates only on strict improvement over the incumbent.
observables: Controller-reported validation HR@10 and its difference from baseline 0, corrected terminal-only control, and incumbent.

steps.expected_observation: A possible HR@10 improvement attributable solely to correcting right-aligned readout; its magnitude is unknown.
steps.instruction: Starting from baseline 0, change only NextItNetModel.score_candidates to select out[0, -1] instead of count_nonzero-1. Preserve candidate scoring, both class architectures, and all eight numeric hyperparameters. Archive this as the corrected terminal-only reference regardless of retention.

steps.condition: Always after slot 1; if slot 1 failed, implement its intended correction directly from baseline 0.
steps.expected_observation: Agreement with slot 1 for right-aligned nonempty histories; disagreement would undermine implementation confidence.
steps.instruction: Use the same baseline architecture and hyperparameters. Replace terminal indexing with the maximum position whose sequence item is nonzero, falling back to the final position for an empty history. Select that output state and preserve the existing candidate scoring interface. This is a prospectively planned equivalent-implementation control.

steps.expected_observation: Reduced HR@10 relative to corrected terminal-only scoring would support the importance of retaining the latest observed event; equal or higher HR@10 would weaken that interpretation.
steps.instruction: From baseline 0, change only scoring readout to the second-most-recent valid output state, using the latest valid state when only one exists and the final state when none exists. Keep all training behavior and hyperparameters fixed. Treat this as a planned recency control.

steps.expected_observation: A two-state mean may improve over the corrected terminal-only reference if modest smoothing helps.
steps.instruction: From baseline 0, change only scoring readout to the uniform mean of the last two valid output states. Exclude padding, use all available valid states for shorter histories, and fall back to the final state for an empty history. Preserve dot-product candidate scoring.

steps.expected_observation: Improvement over the two-state mean would suggest that a somewhat broader recent context helps; deterioration would suggest dilution.
steps.instruction: Use the slot 4 scoring implementation with window size four. Reconstruct from baseline 0 so no retained changes from other slots enter the comparison. Change no other model or hyperparameter behavior.

steps.expected_observation: This wider-window comparison tests whether aggregation gains persist or disappear as older states receive weight.
steps.instruction: Use the same padding-aware uniform aggregation with window size eight, starting from baseline 0 and changing only scoring readout.

steps.expected_observation: Improvement over uniform four-state aggregation would favor emphasizing the newest state while retaining recent context.
steps.instruction: From baseline 0, aggregate the last four valid output states with normalized weights proportional to 0.5 raised to recency rank, where the newest state has rank zero. Preserve the established short-history and empty-history handling and all other behavior.

steps.expected_observation: Comparison with slot 7 tests whether a slower recency decay provides useful context or introduces dilution.
steps.instruction: Repeat the slot 7 intervention from baseline 0 with normalized weights proportional to 0.8 raised to recency rank. Keep window size four and every other setting fixed.

steps.condition: If any successfully scored aggregation candidate in slots 4-8 strictly exceeds the corrected terminal-only reference, follow branch A; otherwise follow branch B. If no corrected reference scored successfully, follow branch B.
steps.expected_observation: Branch A tests the favored window boundary; branch B tests whether smaller departures from terminal-only scoring avoid dilution.
steps.instruction: Branch A: select the highest-HR@10 aggregation candidate, resolving ties by smaller window and then earlier slot. From baseline 0, preserve its weighting rule and use window size three if its window was two, two if four, or sixteen if eight. Branch B: from baseline 0, use a two-state readout weighted 0.9 on the newest valid state and 0.1 on the preceding valid state, renormalizing over available states. Change only scoring readout.

steps.condition: After slot 9, if any aggregation candidate in slots 4-9 strictly exceeds the corrected terminal-only reference, follow branch A; otherwise follow branch B. If no corrected reference scored successfully, follow branch B.
steps.expected_observation: Branch A tests whether reducing aggregation strength improves the best observed rule. Branch B tests a stronger recency emphasis; failure to improve retains uncertainty and provides no support for aggregation gains.
steps.instruction: Branch A: select the highest-HR@10 aggregation candidate, resolving ties by smaller window and then earlier slot. From baseline 0, use a readout equal to 0.5 times the corrected terminal state plus 0.5 times that candidate's aggregate. Branch B: from baseline 0, use a two-state readout weighted 0.98 on the newest valid state and 0.02 on the preceding valid state. Preserve short-history handling, candidate scoring, architecture, and all hyperparameters.
